Either answer makes Schedule B required and knocks the return out (see /flowIsKnockedOut), because the follow-up filings are not supported. Instructions for Schedule B (Form 1040) (2025) p. 3, Line 7a—Question 2: a U.S. person "must file the form if the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeds $10,000 at any time during 2025" (FinCEN Form 114, line 7b country list); p. 2, Part III: "Regardless of whether you are required to file FinCEN Form 114 (FBAR), you may be required to file Form 8938"; p. 3, Line 8: "If you were the grantor of, or transferor to, a foreign trust that existed during 2025, you may have to file Form 3520." Because any "Yes" knocks out, line 7a question 2 and line 7b are never reached on a supported return.

Fact.Name: Unearned income for the Form 8615 test
Fact.Description: Instructions for Form 8615 (2026 draft) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i8615--dft.pdf, Unearned Income: "It includes taxable interest, dividends, capital gains (including capital gain distributions), rents, royalties, pension and annuity income, taxable scholarship and fellowship grants not reported on Form W-2, unemployment compensation, alimony, the taxable part of social security and pension payments". In scope: Form 1040 lines 2b, 3b, 4b, 5b, 6b, 7 (gains only) and Schedule 1 lines 5 (rents and royalties, gains only), 7 and 8 (other income, such as the Alaska PFD).

Fact.Name: Knockout: tax for certain children who have unearned income (Form 8615)
Fact.Description: Form 8615 is not supported. Instructions for Form 8615 (2026 draft) https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i8615--dft.pdf, Who Must File: "1. The child had more than $2,700 of unearned income. 2. The child is required to file a tax return. 3. The child either: a. Was under age 18 at the end of 2026, b. Was age 18 at the end of 2026 and didn't have earned income that was more than half of the child's support, or c. Was a full-time student at least age 19 and under age 24 at the end of 2026 and didn't have earned income that was more than half of the child's support." and the child doesn't file a joint return. TY2026 figure: $2,700 = 2 x $1,350. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf) §4.02, p. 12: "For taxable years beginning in 2026, the amount in § 1(g)(4)(A)(ii)(I), which is used to reduce the net unearned income reported on the child's return that is subject to the "kiddie tax," is $1,350." 26 U.S.C. 1(g)(4)(A)(ii) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1) subtracts that amount plus "the greater of the amount described in subclause (I)" or connected itemized deductions, so net unearned income is more than $0 only above 2 x $1,350; the 2026 draft instructions (title "2026 Instructions for Form 8615") state the same $2,700. 26 U.S.C. 1(g)(2)(A)(ii) brings in an 18-year-old, and a full-time student under 24, only when "earned income ... does not exceed one-half of the amount of the individual's support"; support isn't asked, so an 18-year-old always stops, even with wages. Support and whether a parent was alive aren't asked, so this stops every return that could meet the test: not filing jointly, unearned income (/form8615UnearnedIncome) over $2,700, and the primary filer under 24 at the end of the year, unless 19 or older and answered no to being a student. Form 8814 (a parent's election to report a child's interest and dividends) is optional, so a parent who does not make it files without it.

Fact.Name: Primary filer earned income for the CDCC, before combat pay and dependent care benefits
Fact.Description: #117: the primary filer's line 1 earned income (/primaryFilerEmployerIncomeSubtotalBase) plus net earnings from self-employment (scheduleC /scheduleCNetProfitForEarnedIncome). Every Schedule C business is the primary filer's while a spouse-owned business stops the return (scheduleC /flowKnockoutScheduleCSpouseBusiness). 26 U.S.C. 21(d)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21#d_1): expenses can't exceed "(A) in the case of a taxpayer who is not married at the close of such year, such individual's earned income for such year, or (B) in the case of a taxpayer who is married at the close of such year, the lesser of such individual's earned income or the earned income of his spouse for such year"; 21(e)(1) uses the 32(c)(2) definition of earned income. 2026 draft Instructions for Form 2441 (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-dft/i2441--dft.pdf, SHA-256 7fdecfe193df435542bb452ba108bee011bef7032fda8abe972d6fbd5de233e7), PDF p. 5, lines 4 and 5: "If filing jointly, figure your and your spouse’s earned income separately." and "2. The amount shown on Schedule SE (Form 1040), line 3, minus any deduction you claim on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 15." and "Caution: You must reduce your earned income by any loss from self-employment." A Schedule C loss is not modeled and stops the return when the credit could apply, and a joint return with a Schedule C stops it too until Schedule SE is figured per spouse (scheduleC /flowKnockoutScheduleCEarnedIncomeCredits).
